response:
READING

**Starting point: what does PENNYQUAY actually deliver?**

The undertaking route is not a theoretical risk. It is an observed outcome with two named precedents. Cadgarth (2024) and Nant Elwy (2025) both filed with a dated undertaking and both were renewed for six years. There is no reason to expect Blaenclydach to be treated differently: the Board already knows this intake screen cannot earn a certificate, which is precisely why the undertaking is needed. A six-year renewal from 2028-05-31 expires 2034-05-31. The loan runs to 2039. The bank wrote on 2026-06-22 that a licence term shorter than the loan would put the facility under review. PENNYQUAY does not avoid the bank problem; it almost certainly produces it. The £8,436 outage saving is trivial against a £480,000 facility under review. PENNYQUAY must be assessed as a course that leads, with near-certainty, to a financing crisis.

**Examining the derogation probability under LINTHAUGH**

The Rivers Board decided eleven applications in 2025 in fourteen weeks and granted four. Taken alone, a 36 % grant rate is sobering. But the published record is more informative than the raw fraction: every refusal named a scheme with no dated regulatory driver. That is a categorical distinction, not a marginal one. The Board is saying it will refuse you if you have no regulatory compulsion to act outside the window; it has not said anything against a scheme that does have one. Blaenclydach's dated driver is unambiguous: the abstraction licence renewal must be lodged by 2027-05-31, the renewal file is incomplete without a compliance certificate, the certificate requires the replacement screen, and in-river works cannot lawfully occur in time to install the screen before that deadline under normal rules. That is the argument the derogation application puts. The worst-case reading of the 2025 data is that all four approvals also had dated drivers, making the approval rate for dated-driver schemes 4/4. The most conservative reading is that the Board sometimes approves and sometimes refuses dated-driver applications, in which case the probability is still well above 50 %. Either way, the pattern of published refusals is a strong positive signal for this particular application.

**The deposit risk and the fallback**

The uncomfortable feature of LINTHAUGH is that the deposit (£46,000, non-returnable after 2026-12-01) is committed more than seven weeks before the decision arrives on 2027-01-25. If the Board refuses, that money is gone. The question is what happens next. A refusal on 2027-01-25 leaves eighteen weeks to lodge the renewal, and the July slot can still be secured (Vossbeck confirms by 2027-04-30, within that window). So a refusal under LINTHAUGH produces: £9,000 application fee lost, £46,000 deposit lost, July outage (£8,436), and then the undertaking route — which lands in exactly the same position as PENNYQUAY but with £55,000 in additional sunk costs and the same bank risk.

That is the genuine downside: the worst case for LINTHAUGH is PENNYQUAY plus £55,000.

**Weighing the paths**

| | LINTHAUGH granted | LINTHAUGH refused |
|---|---|---|
| Direct cost | £74,152 | £63,436 |
| Renewal term | 15 years (to 2043) | 6 years (to 2034) |
| Loan term | 2039 | 2039 |
| Bank risk | None | Triggered |

PENNYQUAY: direct cost £8,436, renewal term 6 years (to 2034), bank risk triggered.

The bank risk is not symmetrical. A facility under review on a £480,000 loan dwarfs any of the direct cost differentials. PENNYQUAY makes the bank risk nearly certain. LINTHAUGH, on the strength of the dated-driver evidence, makes it probable (though not certain) that the bank risk is avoided entirely.

The argument for PENNYQUAY reduces to: "The Board might grant undertakings on fifteen-year terms even though the two published precedents show six years." That is possible, but it asks for something the Board has not yet done for any scheme, while simultaneously exposing the business to the bank covenant the instant a six-year renewal is issued. There is no upside in PENNYQUAY that compensates for the near-certain bank trigger.

The argument against LINTHAUGH reduces to: "The Board might refuse despite the dated driver, costing us £55,000 extra and landing us in the same place." That is possible, but the published evidence says the Board does not refuse applicants who have a dated regulatory driver. Paying £74,152 to have a high probability of a fifteen-year renewal and a secured loan is the better gamble when the alternative is paying £8,436 for a near-certain six-year renewal and a facility under review.

**Conclusion**

The decisive comparison is not between the outage costs. It is between a near-certain bank trigger (PENNYQUAY) and a high-probability route to a fifteen-year renewal that keeps the loan out of review (LINTHAUGH). The deposit risk is real but priced correctly given the strength of the dated-driver argument and the severity of the alternative.

---

READING
  PENNYQUAY's undertaking route replicates the Cadgarth and Nant Elwy outcome almost exactly, producing a six-year renewal that expires in 2034 and directly triggers the bank's stated facility-review condition on a £480,000 loan. LINTHAUGH's derogation application rests on a dated regulatory driver — the 2027-05-31 licence-renewal deadline requiring the compliance certificate — of precisely the kind the Rivers Board has never cited against any applicant; a grant produces a fifteen-year renewal covering the loan to 2039. The £74,152 direct cost of a successful LINTHAUGH is far smaller than the financing risk PENNYQUAY makes near-certain, and the fallback if the derogation is refused (eighteen weeks remain to lodge with an undertaking, July slot still available) is the same outcome as PENNYQUAY with £55,000 extra — a worse worst-case, but not a qualitatively different one, and worth accepting given the probability distribution implied by the Board's own published reasoning. The deposit being non-returnable before the decision is the only genuine asymmetry that favours PENNYQUAY, and it is insufficient to outweigh the near-certain bank trigger on the other side.

CALL
  LINTHAUGH

GROUNDS
  PENNYQUAY's undertaking route produces, per the only two published precedents, a six-year renewal that expires before the 2039 loan maturity and thereby triggers the bank's own stated facility-review condition, making PENNYQUAY not a safe course but a near-certain financing crisis, whereas LINTHAUGH's derogation rests on a dated regulatory driver of the exact kind the Rivers Board has never cited against any applicant, offering a high-probability route to a fifteen-year renewal that keeps the loan out of review at a direct cost that is large but bounded and far smaller than the risk PENNYQUAY makes nearly inevitable.
